name: Earnings (Front-Month) Calendar Spread
summary: Sell the expiry that contains the earnings print and buy the next expiry that does not, at the same strike; harvests the fact that the event month's IV crushes far more than the following month's.

legs.strike_rule: ATM, |delta| 0.45-0.55, at the strike nearest the post-earnings expected close (usually just spot). Use puts instead of calls if the put side is tighter or the name pays a dividend in the window - the structure is identical.
legs.dte_rule: first expiry AFTER the earnings date, typically 1-8 DTE at entry
the next expiry that does NOT contain another event; 21-45 DTE, at least 14 days beyond the front

max_profit: Realized the morning after the print if spot opens near the strike: the back month retains most of its value while the front month collapses. Typically 20-60% of the debit; occasionally 100%+ when front IV was extremely elevated.
max_loss: The net debit paid. Realized when the stock gaps beyond roughly 1x the implied move, which flattens the value differential between the two months.
breakevens: Approximately strike +/- (0.6 to 0.9) x the front-month implied move. If the implied move is larger than your breakeven band, the trade has a negative expectancy - skip it.

greeks.gamma: strongly negative across the event - this is the risk
greeks.theta: positive but irrelevant over a 1-day hold; the P&L is vol, not theta
greeks.vega: net positive overall, but decomposed: short front vega (the point of the trade) and long back vega

when_to_use: Only when the term structure is steeply backwardated into the event: front_IV - back_IV >= 8 vol points, ideally >= 12. Best on large, liquid names with a history of the realized move being smaller than the implied move. Do not run it on names with a history of 2x-implied-move gaps (high-beta small caps, biotech binary events, meme names).
typical_dte: front 1-8 DTE (first post-event expiry), back 21-45 DTE
entry_rules: Confirmed earnings date and confirmed that the front expiry contains it and the back expiry contains no second event.
front_IV - back_IV >= 8.0 vol points at the ATM strike.
Front-month implied move (ATM straddle / spot) <= 8%; skip anything above.
Historical check: over the last 8 prints, the median |actual move| must be < 0.8 x the current implied move.
Enter in the last 60 minutes of the session BEFORE the print (between 15:00 and 15:50 ET), never days early - the front IV ramp is the payment.
Strike = the strike nearest spot at entry, |delta| 0.45-0.55.
Net debit <= 1% of equity per unit; maximum 2 earnings calendars open at once.
Combined bid-ask <= 8% of debit; reject wide event-week markets.
LEVEL 3 OK (same-strike, long back covers short front). Single mleg order; long leg first if legging.
management_rules: This is a one-session trade. There is no 'management' - there is an exit the next morning.
Do not adjust, roll, or 'give it time' after the print. The edge is the single IV-crush event.
Do not add size after the print regardless of direction.
If the print is delayed or moved past the front expiry, close the position the same day for whatever it fetches.
exit_rules: Close the FULL spread between 09:45 and 10:30 ET on the session after the print, unconditionally, win or lose. Waiting past 10:30 gives the gamma back.
If the front leg is 0DTE the morning after, the 14:30 ET forced-close rule applies as a hard backstop, but the trade should already be flat by 10:30.
Close the short leg immediately if it goes ITM with extrinsic <= $0.05 - a post-earnings ITM short is an assignment candidate the same day.
Emergency: if the stock gaps more than 1.5x the implied move, close on the open; do not wait for the 09:45 window.
Leg out short-first if the mleg close does not fill within 3 minutes; then work the long.
assignment_risk: The short front leg for one overnight session while it may be deep ITM after the gap. This is the highest per-trade assignment risk in the whole calendar family because the short is nearly expiring and can move deep ITM overnight. The covering long back-month leg means the worst case is a covered stock position, but it must be flattened the same morning.
liquidity_needs: Front expiry OI >= 1,000 and back expiry OI >= 500 at the chosen strike; underlying ADV >= 5M shares; penny or nickel quotes. Event-week spreads widen - measure at entry, not from a stale chain.
common_mistakes: Entering days before the print (paying for the IV ramp instead of selling it); choosing names where the realized move routinely exceeds the implied move; holding past the morning after; using an OTM strike to be directional and then being right about direction but wrong about magnitude; ignoring that the back month also crushes a few points, which eats the theoretical profit.
zero_dte_notes: The front leg is often 0DTE on the morning after the print. Treat that morning as an assignment-risk session: exit by 10:30 ET, hard backstop 14:30 ET.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
